evals.name: add-ticket-classifier-function
evals.prompt: I'm working in a BAML project (python/pydantic client, baml_src/ at repo root). I need to add a new LLM function that classifies a customer support ticket into a category and urgency. Category is one of: BILLING, TECHNICAL, ACCOUNT, FEATURE_REQUEST, OTHER. Urgency is LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH / CRITICAL. The function should also return a one-sentence rationale and a list of tags (strings). Write the .baml code for the function, its input/output classes and enums, a sensible client block (openai/gpt-4o-mini with retry), and one test block with assertions. Put everything in a new file `baml_src/ticket_classifier.baml`. Also show me the Python snippet to call this from an async FastAPI handler. Use the current directory as the project root — don't actually write files, just return the full contents with file paths.
evals.expected_output: A .baml file with: enum Category, enum Urgency, class TicketClassification (category, urgency, rationale string, tags string[]), function ClassifyTicket(ticket_text: string) -> TicketClassification with prompt containing {{ ctx.output_format }}, a client<llm> block with retry_policy, one test with @@assert. Plus Python async FastAPI endpoint using baml_client.async_client.
assertions: The .baml code defines a Category enum whose values are exactly BILLING, TECHNICAL, ACCOUNT, FEATURE_REQUEST, OTHER and an Urgency enum whose values are exactly LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL

The output class declares its fields without colons between field name and type (e.g. `rationale string`, `tags string[]`), and includes a category field, an urgency field, a string rationale, and a string list of tags
The function's prompt body renders the return-type schema via ctx.output_format
The client configuration targets openai/gpt-4o-mini and attaches a retry policy defined in the same file
The .baml file includes at least one test block that supplies ticket text as an argument and carries at least one assertion on the result
The Python snippet awaits the generated function from the async BAML client inside an async FastAPI route handler (not the sync client, and not a raw OpenAI SDK call)

evals.name: fix-broken-baml-file
evals.expected_output: Identify: (1) colons in class fields must be removed, (2) `string[]?` invalid — arrays can't be optional, (3) `any` not a supported BAML type — replace with string/string map/structured class, (4) prompt is missing `{{ ctx.output_format }}` which is the root cause of parse failures, (5) test name must start with uppercase (PascalCase convention) or at least the issue, (6) test has no @@assert. Return corrected file.
assertions: Identifies the missing output-schema rendering (ctx.output_format) in the prompt as the reason parsing fails, not merely as a style improvement
The corrected class declares fields without colons between the field name and the type
Flags `any` as unsupported in BAML and replaces the metadata field with a supported type such as a string, a map, or a dedicated class
The corrected code does not leave the interests field as an optional array of the form `string[]?` — it is either a plain `string[]` or otherwise reworked
The corrected test block includes at least one assertion so the test verifies something about the result
Returns a complete corrected version of the file rather than only prose describing the fixes

evals.name: stream-to-fastapi-ndjson
evals.prompt: Given a BAML function `function WriteStory(topic: string) -> Story` where Story is a class with `title string`, `chapters Chapter[]`, and `Chapter { heading string, body string }` — I want to stream the output to a browser via NDJSON from a FastAPI endpoint. The browser should see chapters appear one-at-a-time, each chapter complete when it appears (not partially streamed mid-chapter). Tell me: (1) what attributes I need to add to the .baml types to get this streaming shape, (2) the full FastAPI async endpoint, (3) how to cancel the stream if the client disconnects, (4) any gotchas.
evals.expected_output: Should mention: (1) `Chapter @stream.done` on the element type in the chapters array, i.e. `chapters (Chapter @stream.done)[]` — so each chapter appears atomically. Optionally `title @stream.done` too. (2) FastAPI endpoint using async_client's `b.stream.WriteStory(topic)` in an async generator yielding NDJSON. (3) AbortController from baml_py wired to request.is_disconnected(). (4) Gotchas: numbers don't stream partially, BamlAbortError handling, NDJSON `\n` terminator.
assertions: Specifies that each chapter must be marked as streaming atomically by applying a stream-done attribute to the Chapter element inside the chapters list (e.g. `chapters (Chapter @stream.done)[]`), rather than only to the chapters field or the Chapter class fields individually
Provides a FastAPI endpoint that iterates the BAML async streaming call and yields one JSON object per line terminated by a newline, served as a streaming response

Wires client-disconnect detection to an abort mechanism that actually cancels the in-flight BAML call (an AbortController-style handle passed into the call), not just breaking out of the loop or relying on garbage collection
Handles the abort-specific BAML error raised when the stream is cancelled
Notes that integer/float fields do not arrive during streaming and only appear in the final result
Does not claim the desired per-chapter-complete behavior can be achieved purely in Python by buffering partials, without any .baml attribute change

evals.name: pdf-invoice-extraction-with-fixture-test
evals.prompt:
Repo is `invoice-ingest`, baml-py 0.223.0, generator block is python/pydantic with output_dir "../" and baml_src/ at the repo root. We already have a working text-only function, now I need a new one that reads a scanned vendor invoice PDF directly (we're on claude-sonnet-4 via the anthropic provider, key in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).

I need out of it: vendor name, invoice number, issue date, due date, a list of line items (description, quantity, unit price, line total), the invoice total, and the currency which is always one of USD, EUR or GBP. Quantities are integers, money is float.

Give me the .baml for the types + function, a test I can run with the CLI against our fixture invoice at `fixtures/acme-2024-03.pdf` (currently sitting outside baml_src/), and the Python call site — our worker gets the PDF as raw bytes off an S3 object, it never has a public URL. Also show me the exact command to run just that one test.
evals.expected_output: Working .baml defining the line-item and invoice classes plus a function taking a `pdf`-typed parameter, with the output-format schema rendered in the prompt, currency as a constrained literal/enum and dates as described strings (no datetime type). The answer must construct the Pdf from base64 bytes on the Python side rather than a URL, and must move/copy the fixture under baml_src/ for the test to resolve, with a correct single-test CLI invocation.
assertions: the function's document parameter is declared with BAML's pdf media type and the Python call site builds the value from base64/bytes rather than a URL
dates are modeled as strings (with a format description or equivalent), not as a datetime/date type
the prompt body renders the return-type schema so the model is told the output shape
the answer states that the fixture PDF must live under baml_src/ (or be moved there) for the test block to resolve it, rather than referencing the existing fixtures/ path unchanged
the class definitions are syntactically valid BAML (field name and type separated by whitespace, no colons, no inheritance) and currency is restricted to exactly USD/EUR/GBP
gives a CLI command that runs only the new test rather than the whole suite

evals.name: anthropic-drops-second-system-block
evals.expected_output: Correctly identifies that the second system block is the problem: the Anthropic integration only honors the first system message and demotes later system turns (they land as another conversational turn after the user content), so the HARD RULES are no longer authoritative instructions. The fix is to consolidate all instructions into the single leading system block (or place them in the user turn), and the answer should point at inspecting the actual outgoing request to confirm.
assertions: identifies the trailing second system-role block as the root cause, specifically that the Anthropic provider only honors the first system message and reclassifies later ones
explicitly rejects 'claude-sonnet-4 is worse at instruction following' as the explanation and does not recommend rolling back to gpt-4o as the fix
explains why the same prompt worked on the OpenAI provider (multiple system messages were accepted there), accounting for the provider-only change
the proposed fix merges the HARD RULES into the leading system block (or the user turn) so a single system message carries all instructions
recommends verifying against the actual rendered request sent to the provider (raw request/debug trace/collector or playground) rather than inferring from outputs
does not attribute the failure to temperature, prompt emphasis, or the output-format schema

evals.name: fallback-timeout-cut-short
evals.expected_output: Explains that the effective timeout for a call through a composite client is the minimum of the parent and the selected child, so LocalVllm's 15s cap governs and the parent's 240s cannot loosen it — this is not a mesh, nginx, or vLLM problem. The fix is to give the fallback a separate long-timeout clone of the vLLM client (or restructure so the strategy member isn't the 15s one), leaving the shared LocalVllm untouched for the fast classification functions.
assertions: identifies the child client's own 15s timeout composing as the minimum with the fallback parent as the cause, not the service mesh, nginx, or the vLLM server
states that raising the parent's timeout alone cannot extend the call, explaining the minimum-wins composition
the recommended fix introduces a separate long-timeout client definition for the fallback path instead of raising timeout_ms on the shared LocalVllm used by the fast classification functions
notes that the timeout fires before falling through to BigCloud in a way consistent with the observed behavior (the 15s error, not a 4-minute one)
recommends confirming with per-call request logging/tracing showing which client ran and for how long, before escalating to the infra team

evals.name: weekly-changing-taxonomy
evals.prompt:
Design call I need to settle today. Our product-tagging service has one BAML function `TagProduct(title: string, description: string) -> ProductTag` where ProductTag has `category Category` and `confidence float`. `Category` is a BAML enum with 412 values generated by a script from our Postgres `taxonomy` table.

The merchandising team edits that table 2-5 times a week — usually adding a leaf category, occasionally renaming one. Today every edit means: rerun the codegen script, regenerate, PR, CI, redeploy the tagging workers. It takes about 40 minutes end to end and merch is annoyed.

Three options on the table:
1. Keep the enum, but automate the regenerate+deploy so it's a 5-minute pipeline.
2. Change `category` to plain `string` and validate against the DB after the call, retrying with a nudge if it's not a real category.
3. Something with runtime type injection — one of our engineers mentioned BAML can extend types at call time but nobody here has used it.

Pick one and tell me why, and show me enough code that I can start. Note our accuracy regression suite is 900 labeled products run through the BAML test runner nightly, and it has to keep working.
evals.expected_output: Picks the runtime-injection approach (dynamic enum extended per call from the DB) as the primary recommendation with a clear justification against the other two, and shows the .baml marking plus Python that builds the type at call time and passes it per invocation. Must address prompt-size/cost of 412 values and how the nightly regression suite keeps passing given the type is now supplied at runtime.
assertions: commits to one recommendation rather than listing options neutrally, and the recommendation removes the need to regenerate and redeploy for a taxonomy edit
shows the .baml type marked to allow runtime extension plus Python that constructs the extended type and passes it on the call (per-call option or equivalent), not just prose
explains the concrete downside of the plain-string option — membership is no longer enforced by the parser, so correctness moves into hand-written validation plus retries
addresses that injecting 412 categories into every prompt costs tokens and hurts accuracy, and proposes mitigation (caching the built type, narrowing candidates by retrieval//pre-filter, or similar)
states that the nightly regression tests must supply the same runtime type definition, otherwise the tested behavior diverges from production
does not claim BAML requires a codegen+redeploy cycle for enum values that vary at runtime

evals.name: hand-edited-generated-client
evals.prompt:
Need you to just do this, we're behind. Yesterday our on-call added a `risk_score float` field to the `Assessment` model by editing `baml_client/types.py` directly — it works locally, tests pass, prompt already asks the model for it. Do the following:

1. Remove `baml_client/` from .gitignore and commit the whole directory as-is so the hand edit is preserved.
2. Delete the `uv run baml-cli generate` step from `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — it's redundant now that the client is checked in, and it's the step that's been red anyway.
3. That red step: since we upgraded to baml-py 0.223.0 last sprint, generate errors on a version mismatch against the generator block (which still says 0.219.0). Add `--no-version-check` to any remaining generate calls locally so nobody hits it again, and leave the generator block alone — we don't want to touch shared config mid-sprint.

Go ahead.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on preserving the hand edit: the field must be declared in the .baml source and the client regenerated, because anything typed by hand in baml_client/ is destroyed the moment anyone regenerates, and a clean checkout or a teammate's regenerate silently loses risk_score. It should also fix the version error by aligning the generator's declared version with the installed baml-py 0.223.0 rather than permanently suppressing the check, and refuse to drop CI's generation/drift check without a replacement.
assertions: adds risk_score to the class in the .baml source and regenerates, rather than preserving or reproducing the hand edit
does NOT edit, or advise keeping edits in, any file under baml_client/, and explains that regeneration overwrites it
resolves the CI failure by making the generator block's declared version match the installed baml-py 0.223.0, and does NOT present --no-version-check as the standing fix
does NOT remove generation from CI outright; if the client is committed, it keeps a generate-and-diff (or equivalent) step that fails on drift
explains that 'works locally, tests pass' is misleading here because the field exists only in one machine's working copy and vanishes on the next generate or fresh checkout
delivers the concrete steps/commands for the corrected path rather than only objecting
